Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5351; undecaying (in essence or continuance):--not (in-, un-)corruptible, immortal.
BiblicalUsage: The adjective for what cannot decay. At the last trump the dead shall be raised incorruptible in 1 Corinthians 15:52, and Peter says our inheritance is incorruptible, undefiled, and fadeth not away, reserved in heaven in 1 Peter 1:4. We ourselves are born again, not of corruptible seed but of incorruptible, by the word of God in 1 Peter 1:23 — and the word belongs first to God Himself, the King eternal, immortal, invisible in 1 Timothy 1:17.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word steadies me when everything around me wears out. Bodies age, goods rust, and even good things fade — but the inheritance, the new birth, and the God who gives them do not decay. If what I am building on is incorruptible, then the life built on it will outlast the grave.
